metrics: Detector CPM, held-out test (122 scans, raw DICOM)
Malignancy AUC on correctly detected nodules
Patient-level malignancy AUC from raw CT
Mean time per scan (Kaggle T4 GPU)
limitations: Research prototype. Not a medical device and not validated for clinical use.
Trained and tested only on LIDC-IDRI (patients 0001-0600); no external hospital data.
'Malignancy' means radiologists' visual suspicion score (1-5), not biopsy-proven cancer.
Ground truth = nodules >= 3 mm marked by >= 3 of 4 readers; smaller or less-agreed nodules are not scored.
The classifier never saw non-nodules: about 1 in 5 false alarms is rated >= 50% malignant.
Original classifier checkpoint was chosen on some of the test patients, so its numbers are optimistic.
Probabilities are poorly calibrated (ECE 0.24); MC-dropout spread is small and only weakly flags errors.
Malignancy accuracy falls if the nodule centre is off by several mm (AUC 0.73 at 6 mm).
